title: Declarative runbook language with safe dry-run, policy sandbox, and reversible checkpoints
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Ship a declarative runbook format (YAML-first) that makes support flows auditable and machine-validated, supports a non-destructive dry-run mode, and enforces side-effect policies via a policy sandbox. Background: Current runbooks are a mix of ad-hoc scripts and procedural notes which makes automated simulation, validation, and safe execution difficult. This increases oncall friction and leads to sometimes irreversible manual fixes. This initiative aims to reduce blast radius by providing: 1) a typed declarative syntax for common primitives (query, patch, rollout, wait, escalate), 2) a dry-run simulator that exercises control flow and telemetry without mutating production, 3) reversible checkpoints (transaction-like snapshots) for multi-step remediation, and 4) a policy sandbox that blocks or flags unsafe primitives (eg: bulk DB writes, privilege escalation) unless allowed by a scoped override workflow. Non-goals: Replacing all ad-hoc scripts on day one; building a full DSL interpreter that duplicates all shell capabilities. Approach: - Design a compact YAML schema with typed params and annotations for replay/simulate. - Implement a simulator that calls read-only shadow endpoints and validates side-effecting steps against a policy engine. - Add checkpoints implemented as idempotent compensating steps where possible and fallbacks where not. - Integrate with Console to show dry-run traces, replay diffs, and required approvals. - Provide a migration tool that wraps existing scripts into the new format with TODO stubs. See acceptance_criteria for testable targets.
acceptance_criteria: YAML schema v1 published and documented in Confluence with examples for query/patch/rollout/wait/escalate
Dry-run simulator can execute 90% of internal runbook primitives against shadow/test endpoints with no production writes
Policy sandbox blocks high-risk operations by default and emits clear remediation guidance when blocking occurs
Console shows annotated dry-run traces (per-step status, simulated diffs, affected resources) for at least 3 canonical playbooks
Implementation includes a reversible checkpoint primitive with a documented compensation strategy and one end-to-end validated runbook using checkpoints
Migration script converts at least 5 legacy scripts into declarative stubs and flags manual steps for human review
